newsitem.title: JAPAN: Former copper star Hamanaka pleads guilty.
newsitem.headline: Former copper star Hamanaka pleads guilty.

text.p: Former Sumitomo copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka pleaded guilty on Monday to charges that he engaged in fraud and forgery as part of a massive trading scheme that cost his former employer $2.6 billion.

Hamanaka entered the guilty pleas at the start of his trial at the Tokyo District Court on charges of forgery and defrauding trading house Sumitomo Corp. The charges carry a penalty of up to 15 years in prison.

Hamanaka, who spent all of his professional life at Sumitomo, was considered the most powerful player in the global copper market, feared by other traders for the influence he wielded over the market.
He was fired last June by the company for what it said were years of unauthorised trading. Sumitomo estimates the improper trading cost the firm $2.6 billion.

But the criminal case does not answer the bigger question of whether Hamanaka manipulated the world copper market and, if so, who benefited. While those questions are being investigated by U.S. and British regulators, Japanese authorities say that since the copper deals all took place overseas, they are not involved.
